name: Creative Superskills (Claude plugin)
summary: Creative Factories' Claude plugin: First Draft (brief to 3 on-brand Figma proposals), AdGen (finished static ads), Ad Resizer, Figma Transcreation, and deck builders for Figma Slides, Google Slides and PowerPoint. Hard launch + live demo was scheduled for AI Briefly 2026-11-11 (that session was cancelled).
how_to_use: Claude > Customize > Plugins > Browse > 'Your organisation' > Creative Superskills > Install. Enablement sessions 18 Nov (EMEA) and 25 Nov (LATAM).

name: AI-built visual system (images, video, vibe-coding)
summary: Jon Saude walked through building a full visual system with AI end to end: image generation, video generation and vibe-coding.

name: Motion DNA (After Effects plugin + Claude MCP)
summary: Motion DNA: an After Effects plugin connected to Claude through MCP (built with Opus 5.5), with a motion library, predefined animation behaviours and granular easing control. Presented by Gian Orsi and Aaron Amortegui at AI, Briefly #67 (2026-10-28); the Sana course embeds the Motion DNA page.
how_to_use: Watch the #67 recording on Sana and open the Motion DNA page; testing and questions in #motion_dna_mcp_testing.

name: Higgsfield: From Zero to Motion
summary: Tomi Foldes' beginner workflow for Higgsfield (#66): use the free Supercomputer chat generator (avoid the pricey Astra model), build a character, run Apps > Character Sheet to lock it (angles, lighting, skin detail) and feed the sheet back for consistent images and video; Fitting Room for wardrobe, Canvas (node-based, like Flora) and Marketing Studio templates (upload product + avatar, recreate). Comes with a one-page Camera Cheat Sheet (27 presets, prompt order camera move > subject > action > setting > lighting > lens > mood, one move per clip, lens guide). Superside has no Higgsfield licence yet; Manuel Berbin noted the same orchestration can be done with Krea/Flora + Claude Opus + MCPs + a local repo.
how_to_use: Download the Camera Cheat Sheet from the Sana course and paste it into Claude/ChatGPT to write prompts. Higgsfield Supercomputer can also be connected to Claude via MCP. For access on a specific project, ask your manager/GM; otherwise use Krea or Flora.

name: Claude Code for Design
summary: Claude Code as a design production engine. #64 (Tor Egil Fusdahl, 2026-10-07): starting from one prompt that used the Superspace internal MCP to list Brand Models, Tor produced V1s for 24 client projects in 12 days (668 videos, 392 PDFs, 70 decks) with ~20-word messages and no code; outputs are editable Figma, HTML, JS animations exportable to After Effects, PowerPoint and Google Slides (Oura ebook, Zipline route animation, Virgin Red 17-module email system, Mojave summit deck, Gusto ads); Figma comments are turned into edits by Claude; four studio pilots (Burton 99 assets in under an hour, Sesame 17 email modules in under 5 h). #65 'Dr. Stragentlove' (Manuel Berbin, 2026-10-15): move from Cowork to Claude Code; a repo with CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, context/, learnings/, skills/, projects/, outputs/; MCPs (Krea, Flora, Superside MCP, Chrome, Figma, Canva, Pencil, Blender, ArtCraft); every output is code; save and reinject feedback as learnings (global > client > format > project); a good brief = context + instructions + output spec.
how_to_use: Watch #64 and #65 on Sana. Tor's Get-started guide is in Notion (linked from the deck); channels #claude-mint and #motion-commotion. Download Manuel's 'stragentlove-starter' repo template (see the separate item).

name: Before. After. This. That.
summary: Lauren Coetzee's retrospective (#63, 2026-09-30): from Superside's first AI library (GroupM, built in Midjourney) to today. AI didn't make work faster so much as make us think harder; we moved from designing to directing; references beat prompts; AI loves specificity (hex codes, lens, lighting); AI is a talented intern who takes everything literally; taste and creative direction matter more than ever.

name: AI video production workflow
summary: AI video production pipeline (#60, 2026-09-09). Three ways to drive a shot (prompt only, first + last frame, image/video reference). Pre-production ships as one package: sketch storyboard, character contact sheets, location plates, props, locked visual style. Production: 1:1 base images expanded to every ratio, hero ratio first, every crop checked; fix framing with Smart Objects, flips and crops rather than regenerating. Post: overshoot (5 s for a 3 s need) and trim; multiple references with one job each (strip the plate, feed Seedance 360-degree car turnaround videos, name roles with @image#); borrow camera moves from a reference clip; Runway video expand as fallback. Sign it off as a still, then animate.

name: Hybrid workflows (Corelight illustration library, Aderant 'Wolfie' mascot)
summary: Marie Gimenez's hybrid AI + traditional workflows. #54 (2026-07-29), Corelight: building an article illustration library from headline-only briefs: Krea Moodboards 'Analyze board', reverse-engineer the colour style to a B&W sketch style, Krea Nodes + Nano Banana Pro sketches, a Claude skill that generates concepts/prompts from the article title, a Superside Brand Model trained on the sketch style for B&W directions, then Figma vectorize, brand palette and noise. #61 (2026-09-16), Aderant 'Wolfie': mascot redesign in five phases (moodboard; morphology and sketches with line-art redraw prompts, turntables incl. Illustrator's AI turntable, character sheet, pose prompts; colour and style; pose library; Brand Model with a NAME + EMOTION + ACTION + @Brand Model prompt formula). Lesson: use AI when it earns its place; every project earns its own workflow.
how_to_use: Watch #54 and #61 on Sana; prompts are in the decks.

name: /daily-planning skill
summary: /daily-planning Claude skill (#59 'Daily Habit', 2026-09-02): every morning surfaces the top 5 priorities tagged Make / Unblock / Decide with reasons, threads and emails you'd miss, your projects (needs action / pending info / not urgent), billable vs non-billable hours against target, the day's meetings and deadlines with double-bookings flagged, and buttons that act (draft reply, clear, route). Integrates Slack, Gmail, Asana, Superspace and Calendar. Roadmap: Staffing & Booking Engine, /project-planning, creative admin skills, automations. Team: Careth Colmenarez, Magnolia Flynn, Michal Stangret, Matteo Rostagno.
how_to_use: Claude > Customize > Browse > Plugins > 'Your Organisation' tab > + to install (Creative Starter Pack). Run /daily-planning, or ask Claude to schedule it as a morning routine. Support: #creative-skills-support.

name: AI Bootcamp production workflows
summary: AI Bootcamp behind the scenes. #33 (Natasha Prinsloo with Luc Barreto and Daniela Riveros, 2026-02-25): Kaseya Connect 2026 event creative 'Systems in Sync' built in Krea Nodes (LLM call > line splitter > Nano Banana Pro abstract library; LLM-written persona prompts for a character library; pose and background swaps; phone-screen mockups; Kling loops; Topaz + Photoshop finishing). #57 (Vitória Borba, 2026-08-19): June hybrid bootcamp briefs: Sprout Social (create consistent AI 'models' first; screen-mockup prompt 'there is a glass over the UI') and a fictional Dropbox AI conference (Flora flower key visual with short prompts, a vibe-coded badge maker for an event check-in totem, Seedance motion tests, a Flora mockup workflow; a daily game plan with Claude). #58 (Karolina Razuri, 2026-08-26): 'Trial, Error, Repeat': strong moodboard, colour palette and photo direction first; stay organised.

name: Keeping Color True (NB2 batch color-correction script)
summary: Fixes colour drift in batches of Nano Banana 2 generations; shows the ComfyUI custom-node solution plus a script anyone can use, with measured per-generation colour variation (#56).

name: The Skill Drop / Creative Skill Marketplace
summary: #55 (Matteo Rostagno, 2026-08-05): after the Hackathon, solutions are being centralised into a Creative Skill Marketplace, the 'core creative OS'. 'The Skill Drop' becomes a monthly AI, Briefly edition on new skills with their creators as guests. Plugin packages per type of work act as wrappers (first set: Quality boosters from TPD, Creative Starter Pack, /skill-gallery finder); independent skills live in the Superside skill directory; a Shared Directory tracks entries and flags duplicates; better connectors are coming (Superspace, Brand Brain, Canva, Figma, Krea, Flora).
how_to_use: Claude > Customize > Browse > Plugins > 'Your Organisation' tab > + to install. Keep sharing in #everyone-can-build; support in #creative-skills-support.

name: Claude + Figma AI: Better Together
summary: Guilherme Fidélio's 'Design AI Companion' (#53, 2026-07-22), the next step after the Figma MCP + Codex design-system companion: Figma AI + Claude audit a screen or flow with categorised findings, turn findings into implementation instructions, make on-canvas fixes with real components, populate realistic content, run accessibility passes at scale, check design-system compliance across a file, remember project context across sessions, and connect to Slack, Asana and Drive.

name: Superside Brand Models (Figma/FigJam plugin)
summary: Superside Brand Models: custom image models trained on a client's visual DNA (10-50 on-brand images, or an AI-built dataset), used in Figma/FigJam through the Superside Brand Models plugin and client-facing in Superspace. #17 (Manuel Berbin, 2025-10-01) positioned it as brief enabler, brainstorming and communication tool, medium-level production and an AI Prompt Assistant; models are trained on FAL.ai (SOC 2, isolated FLUX LoRAs, no base-model training) and priced at ~$635-665 for model only or ~$3,177-3,447 with dataset creation (4.1 plans). #36 (2026-03-25) new Brand Model setup with Brand Brain. #46 'What's new' (Manuel Berbin, Pedro Brasil, 2026-06-03): queue, recycle prompt, auto-enhanced prompts, positives and negatives in the dataset description as guardrails, more models (Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image 2, Luma Uni 1, Seedream 5 Lite), image reference, and context layering (OnePay: three Brand Models blended). #52 'Brand Model Updates and Skillpilled' (2026-07-15).
how_to_use: In Figma run the 'Superside Brand Models' plugin (or use Superspace). Tag @YourBrandModel in prompts. Help: any AICD/AIACD and #brand-models-support.

links.label: #17 deck (Oct 2025, incl. pricing and data privacy)

name: Brand Brain & Superspace 2.0
summary: Special edition: Phillip Maggs live-demoed Superspace 2.0 and the Superside Brand Brain; Manuel Berbin walked through the new Brand Model setup.

name: Marqeta 3D icon render automation (vibe-coded Blender add-on + Blender MCP)
summary: Marqeta team (Javier Velazquez, Sara Popov, with Ara, Ale, Sam, Margot) vibe-coded a Blender add-on that turns SVG icons into controlled 3D renders (template, choose SVG or folder, preview, batch render), built with Claude/Cursor and the Blender MCP (#51, 2026-07-08). Path A (generative AI loop: cloud compute, inconsistent) vs Path B (specialist tool + AI-assisted automation: local, deterministic, near-zero marginal cost, reusable by the client). The pattern applies to Unity, TouchDesigner, Unreal, Figma, After Effects, C4D and Three.js.
how_to_use: Deck includes the initial add-on prompt template and a video on installing the Blender MCP in Claude.

name: personal-voice-builder skill
summary: Teaches Claude to write like you: reads your real Slack messages, maps your 'gears', register by audience and writing fingerprints, then outputs an installable skill, reference file and analysis report. Presented by Phillip Maggs (Senior Director of AI Product) at the #50 special edition (2026-07-01), alongside Kae Neskovic (GM of Sky), community awards and the #50 Creative Challenge winners.
how_to_use: In Claude type /personal-voice-builder; it interviews you.

name: Figma Make for Dummies
summary: Gabrielle Moura (#49, 2026-06-24), in her second week: when Nano Banana was down and models couldn't produce a consistent textured-gradient system, she built a gradient-generator tool in Figma Make instead (MVP in under 30 minutes, about 2 hours total; showing an example frame fixed the style), then used it to create the '_thread' event visual system. Message: don't be intimidated by Figma Make.

name: The Cult of Notebook
summary: Delisa Govender (#48, 2026-06-17) on NotebookLM: RAG over your own vetted sources instead of a guessing LLM. One notebook per project or brand as the source of truth (up to 150M words), turn sources into podcasts, video, flashcards and presentations, ingest YouTube, websites, Drive and pasted text, and share notebooks. Rules: bring your own sources, your own voice (ChatGPT is better for tone), and patience. Suggested flow: brief > sources > notebook > content > refine TOV in ChatGPT > share.

name: Figma Agents
summary: Rafael 'Raga' Costa (#47, 2026-06-10) on the Figma AI Agent: a baseline agent chat that sees the canvas, plus a per-element agent (blue star on any selection). Demo: a website and four social posts for the Superside Consulting AI Academy podcast from the logo, a JSON brand-guidelines prompt and imagery. Watch for brand drift; Figma uses its own image model by default (partner models like Nano Banana/GPT must be picked manually). Available in Superside Figma accounts.

name: Skala: internal scoping tool (Built for How We Work: From Claude to Figma to Production)
summary: Careth Colmenarez (#45, 2026-05-27) built 'Skala', an internal web-project scoping tool that replaces the scoping spreadsheet (thousands of scopes a year), alone in one week: Prompt > Compare (Claude vs Cursor) > Refine in Figma > Handoff > Ship. It has an admin panel to edit cost logic without code (Notion/Supabase backend) and reads UI components from Figma via MCP. Claude is better at planning and foundations, Cursor at executing defined plans; look and feel still needs Figma refinement. 'Stop building for a thousand users, start building for ten.'

name: Design Systems at Scale with Figma MCP + Codex
summary: Guilherme Fidélio's 'Design System AI Companion' for Vail Resorts (#44, 2026-05-20): 36 brands, multiple stakeholders, two channels. Figma MCP connected to Codex with Cursor as the interface, with skills per channel, recorded rules and guidelines, and decision logging. It extracts brand type and colour in minutes, creates accessible colour ramps, assists documentation, reviews pages for design-system adherence and runs DS audits.

name: From Nodes to Image (Flora workflow)
summary: Julia Calabrese (#43, 2026-05-13): back-to-basics node workflow built live: reference image > LLM node > isolate each prompt > image node. Flora project shared for reuse.

name: Vibecoding + Figma MCP for email production
summary: Miguel Leça (#42, 2026-05-06): the vibe-coding landscape (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, v0, Stitch, Replit, Lovable, Pencil.dev, Paper, Figma Make, Claude Design), an AI maturity ladder (Explorer > Practitioner > Integrator > Architect > Steward), Agent Skills (skills.sh, obra/superpowers) and MCPs. Demo: an agent analyses an email screenshot, maps its structure, gets the copy and assembles the email in Figma from design-system components via the Figma Console MCP.

name: The Playground Mindset (Walter Hagen seasonal AI workflows)
summary: Flavio Treiger (#41, 2026-04-29): stop gambling with AI (slot-machine prompting) and start playing: break the work into blocks and change one variable at a time. Case: Dick's Sporting Goods / Walter Hagen full-AI shoot: 9 AI-generated characters, 60+ real SKUs and props, 1 location, 39 shots, 9 scenes, 9 creatives, built as an 'Incredible Machine'.

name: Directed, Not Generated
summary: Manuel Huertas (#40, 2026-04-22): AI has no taste, culture or point of view; you do. The moodboard is the brief and references are input. Inspiration sources (flim.ai, eyecannndy, cosmos.so, shotdeck, are.na, aicandy.be, godly.website). Case: Peruvian street-racing film 'Correcaminos' (mototaxis) with a Weavy workflow using Krea Nano Banana, where LLMs translate cultural knowledge into prompts. Stack: Nano Banana 2/Pro, Z-Image Turbo, Luma Uni-1, Kling 3, Seedance 2, Switch X, Suno/Artlist, Claude, Magnific, SAM3. Voted 'most inspiring session' at #50.

name: The Incredible Bulk
summary: Juan Dupouy (#39, 2026-04-15): a client loved its Brand Model but didn't want to prompt each image, so the team bulk-generated 300 on-brand images. Weavy workflow: LLM call (Gemini 3 Pro) locks the style from the dataset; a second LLM call analyses camera angles and lenses; Prompt Variables + an LLM produce random scene prompts; an Array node splits them, List nodes pick each one and a Prompt Concatenator joins style + camera + scene. Each run yields 10 images; rerun to re-randomise. Diversify the dataset (all outputs had red cars). Extends to video prompts with Seedance 2.0.

name: Seedance 2.0 launch
summary: Rafael 'Raga' Costa (#38, ~2026-04-08): Seedance 2.0 (ByteDance) is available in Superside's Krea accounts: multi-shot frame-consistency reasoning, cinematic editing from one prompt, up to 12 multimodal references (image, text, video), strong physics, multi-character action, SFX/music/dialogue in one prompt, up to 2K and 15 s; >90% usable on the first prompt. Example uses a timecoded prompt written with a ChatGPT prompt assistant. Limits: reference images with faces or recognisable IP are blocked, and it burns credits. Best for product and prompt-based videos.

name: Audiovisual Repository
summary: Julian Garcia's Audiovisual Repository session (#37, ~2026-04-01). The Sana course holds only the recording (no transcript or deck), so details are not captured here.

name: Ultra-high-resolution AI images for print & brochures
summary: Pedro Brasil and Helena Figueiredo (POD4, #35, Mar 2026): why AI images fail in print (a product at ~10% of a 4K frame gets only ~400 px; upscalers stretch pixels). Muse headband: give GPT a PDF of the product's characteristics, generate the product close-up first, then composite it upscaled into the scene. Clara-Tee (Orasis brochure, 100% AI character): Nano Banana Pro 4K, Topaz Gigapixel, Magnific and native upscales all lost identity; the fix is 'AI Zoom Reconstruction': generate the scene, ask Nano Banana to zoom into the face for a new high-detail crop, composite it back and expand in Photoshop.

name: Cinematic AI motion (JSON prompts, shot lists, frame schematics) & AI animation
summary: Gian Orsi (AI Motion Lead). #16 'Control Tips' (2025-09-24): video prompts of 3-6 sentences in film vocabulary, prompt + init image enhanced by an LLM, control with JSON (Seedream Pro), JSON + shot list, frame schematics (red instructions drawn on the first frame, Veo 3) and motion capture (Wan 2.2); 'alchemy': refine AI base material with editing and post. #34 'Once upon a time... A story of animation' (2026-03-04): lessons from cel, multiplane and rigging applied to hybrid 2D: prepare Illustrator assets for AI motion, composite AI-animated characters with vectors and an After Effects 3D camera, retime with motion curves; 80-100 hours saved on rigging and animation.

name: Merch Express x Krea Nodes
summary: Emmanuel Cantón (#31, 2026-02-04): three embroidered baseball-cap designs with mockups for a company retreat in 10 days with thin guidelines. Krea Nodes workflow: place the design, make it look embroidered, build a custom cap mockup, then put the cap on a person; fixes were a stronger position reference and stating what to keep. The shared workflow was reused by the creative and co-CL.

name: Brands, AI, and the Art of Not Messing It Up
summary: Bianca Pieterse (#32, 2026-02-11): spotting AI-faked brands, seven brand trust signals (real founder photo, proof-of-life social content, active socials, Google reviews, a mix of product images, influencers, copy with personality), and questions to ask before using AI (would another brand's output be interchangeable? is AI the right tool or just the most available?). Checklist: trust and honesty, human experience, stakes, brand perception. 'You can automate a lot, but trust isn't one of them.'

name: Krea Nano Banana Elements
summary: Manuel Berbin (#30, 2026-01-28): 'context is everything'. Vision models cross-reference images well, so consistency is about supplying context (images + instructions). Chat interfaces fragment context; node workflows are granular but slow to rewire. Krea's Nano Banana Elements give reusable 'context capsules' with chat-like speed; tie-in with the Brand Models Figma plugin.

name: Node-based platforms: Krea vs Flora vs Weavy vs ComfyUI
summary: Juan Dupouy (#29 'Gnomed Based Platforms', 2026-01-21): Krea and Flora are easiest and cloud-collaborative, ComfyUI gives the deepest control (local), Weavy is precise and integrates with Figma; Krea covers multi-modal output and is the one everyone at Superside can use. Demo (Dexter/Evangelion mecha): image reference > GPT-5 > Nano Banana Pro > GPT-5 video prompt > Kling 2.6, Suno music. Tips: make workflows replicable and understandable. Voted 'most creative session' at #50.
how_to_use: Open the shared Krea Nodes workflow and duplicate it.

name: Kickoff to Kickass
summary: Kickoff constraints and final QC (fixing hallucinations) as the two moments that define AI project success; split complex prompts into structured steps with references.

name: The Contact Sheet Cheat (AI consistency)
summary: Cristian Rojas on character consistency. #15 'How to achieve... Consistency' (2025-09-17): an AI-humans/UGC demo broken down for continuity errors; prompts written by an LLM; Seedream (up to 6-8 references) and Nano Banana, also inside Photoshop via a plugin; first/last frames in Kling; start with the cheapest model and change model after 5-6 failed tries; scope AI projects realistically (solo demo took 15 h generation + 7 h post). #27 'The Contact Sheet Cheat' (2026-01-07): multi-shot consistency for AI video via contact sheets, with a tool ladder: Level 1 Krea 'Contact Sheet App', Level 2 a custom GPT / Gemini Gem to iterate the prompt, Level 3 the Krea Nodes 'Shot Builder' workflow (character sheet, location and composite groups).
how_to_use: Use the Contact Sheet App in Krea (type a brief, optionally add a character reference); for more control, the Shot Builder workflow in Krea Nodes. Links are in the #27 deck.

name: AI in immersive work & MCPs
summary: Manuel Palenque (#25 'Building Tools, Not Just Results', 2025-12-03), from the immersive/spatial team: be creative about workflows, not just results. MCP as an open standard that gives AI context on any tool (Figma, After Effects, Blender); naming conventions give AI more context; still exploratory; AI can explain someone's intricate project.

name: AI-Briefing tool (Using AI to write and read a creative brief)
summary: Preview of an AI-Briefing tool creating executable, personalised briefs via context engineering.

name: Brand mascot feasibility test
summary: Francisco Frigerio (#22 'Building a 3D AI Brand Mascot', 2025-11-12): feasibility test for a 3D construction-worker mascot for Simple Supports & Fixings (bobblehead vs proportionate): explore body type, stylisation, proportions, poses and hair with Krea Flux; pose variations in Midjourney with image prompt, style reference and Omni Reference; post-production in Photoshop and Krea. Team: Marcelo Pelica, Helena Figueiredo.

name: Photoshop + Nano Banana
summary: Juan Sebastián Rivera: Photoshop + Nano Banana compositing (2025-11-05). This session is not in the Sana collection (no numbered course found).

name: Turning AI constraints into creative leverage
summary: Piotr Smietana (#20, 2025-10-22): build video ad concepts around AI's limits (short unstable clips, awkward motion, drift). Four Superside examples: a mockumentary about 'Nathan the creative hero' (5 h), a Q4 'Breaking News' parody where style drift reads as different channels, a Meta hook using Wan 2.5 water transformation, and a stop-motion-style action-figure campaign. Takeaways: start with the flaw, pick a forgiving format, keep AI in the margins, ground ideas in truth, humour gives permission, direct like an editor. Voted 'most viewed session' at #50.

name: Visual to Text prompting
summary: Pedro Brasil (#19, 2025-10-15): stop depending on image references, describe them. Direct references can make results generic; train yourself to translate what you see into words, using GPT to structure it. Workflow: choose an image > describe it with the 'Image to text prompt' custom GPT > refine the prompt yourself > generate and iterate. Use references for character/object consistency and technical accuracy; avoid them when exploring.
how_to_use: Use the 'Image to text prompt' custom GPT (link).

name: Upsampling & Upkeeping (Topaz, Face Enhancer)
summary: Julian Garcia (#18 'Upsampling Upkeeping', 2025-10-08): upscaling with Topaz and Face Enhancer. The Sana deck is image-only, so details come from the Slack recap.

name: Mix Tooling (GPT + Sora + Nano Banana in Krea + Weavy)
summary: Chaining tools: GPT for first character draft and re-style, Sora for expressions, Nano Banana in Krea for scenarios; Weavy + GPT JSON prompt structures + Krea for scalable personas (Schneider Electric).

name: Understanding CIM (Custom Image Models)
summary: Jun Okida (#12, 2025-08-27): a custom image model is a LoRA layer on a base model; its superpower is guided variation, not 1:1 consistency, so align client expectations. Good for styles, objects, characters, backgrounds and abstract brand assets, and for applying a photo style (colour grade). Build datasets by naming the style elements (colour, lens, light) since clients often can't; prompts still override dataset diversity. In Krea: Train, then Style > Private, same base model, set weight. Producers: decide between asking for more brief detail or budgeting exploration.
how_to_use: Krea > Train (upload 12+ images) > in image generation pick the same base model > Style > Private > apply with a weight.

name: AI video in action / end-to-end AI video production
summary: Manuel Berbin's AI video sessions. #8 'AI Video Tips and tricks' (2025-07-23): cheap, controllable video with Seedance in Krea instead of Veo 3: always image-to-video, prompt camera + action, use Seedance Lite first/last frames (new angles from Flux Kontext or Runway Gen-4 References) for orbits and morphs, and edit with ellipses instead of chasing one perfect shot; after 2-3 failed attempts change approach. #10 'End-to-end video production' (2025-08-13): a fake 'Archon' car commercial in about 16 hours: ChatGPT as co-pilot for insight, script and prompts; Veo 3 shots; Seedance interpolation for the car; ElevenLabs Voice Design (screen-recorded ~40 voice clips); Suno cover of a hummed rough score; a tight edit.

name: Achieving consistency with AI
summary: Manuel Berbin (#7 'On consistency', 2025-07-16): consistent product imagery from phone photos. ChatGPT/Sora is good for stylised character consistency but breaks small labels; Flux Kontext gives natural results but distorts small text; Runway Gen-4 References preserves logos and text best (more cinematic look). Always colour-correct (Camera Raw; avoid the 'ChatGPT-cheap' look). Video: Kling 2.1 (pricey) vs Seedance Pro 1080p (cheaper), Seedance Lite with first/last frame.
how_to_use: Step-by-step workflows (post-production, Sora) in the Figma 'AI-Powered Workflows' file linked from the course.

name: Better prompts & Meta prompting
summary: Manuel Berbin. #9 'Better Promptz' (2025-07-30): JSON prompting demystified: models read text, not JSON, but structure (categories, parameters, values) and granularity help. Uses: extract a JSON style prompt from an image to restyle anything consistently, build character/icon collections, and timecoded video direction (Veo 3); works best with LLM-linked image models (ChatGPT image, Gemini) and Seedream; Flux Kontext prefers short prompts. #11 'Meta prompting' (2025-08-20): prompt your prompts (ask the LLM to research best practices for a model, e.g. Flux Kontext or Seedance, then write the prompt), context engineering (show images and docs), use the LLM as a creative-process co-pilot (dump the messy brief, 'optimize this prompt', work in stages); GPT-5 branding-in-20-minutes demo; reusable co-pilot prompt template in the deck.

name: Train your own Krea model (+ Italian brainrot)
summary: Júlio Aymoré. #4 'Julio around the world' (2025-06-25): train a Krea custom Flux model on 20-40 everyday selfies (Train > character, set a trigger word) and generate yourself anywhere; used it for editorial portraits and a LinkedIn video. Krea access: log in with Google and switch to the Superside workspace, which holds the credits. #6 'Italian brainrot' (2025-07-09): AI on social media (Italian brainrot, Cats Olympics with Veo 3/Hunyuan, AI fake-news vlogs; Forbes: 71% of social images are AI-generated); challenge to make sketches with Veo 3.
how_to_use: Krea > Train > upload photos > set the trigger word > train; then generate with that model and include the trigger word. Step-by-step in the Figma 'AI-Powered Workflows' file.

name: Show, don't tell: multi-model image workflow (launch session)
summary: The first AI, Briefly (#3 'The SKA legend', 2025-06-18). Manuel Berbin on why Superside gave everyone ChatGPT + Krea (tool-agnostic workflows): AI is an autocomplete, so close the gap with image references (show, don't tell) and divide and conquer across models. Demo: ChatGPT for a base composition from references, a Krea Flux model trained on his face (trigger word) to swap identity, Krea Edit to refine; a video screenshot is also an image; a rough Photoshop composite plus Flux Kontext material swaps. Assignment: a Y2K fisheye profile picture.
how_to_use: Watch #3; the references used are linked in the deck.

name: Product-in-scene with Flux Kontext (rough montage + simple prompt)
summary: Lucia Quiroga (#5 'On cats and beds', 2025-07-02): place a client product exactly as-is into a new scene with Flux Kontext Pro in Krea. Make a quick rough montage (cut-out subject on the product, no shadows), then a short prompt using the formula Subject + Action + Product (the reference) + Setting + Vibe; Kontext fixes pose, shadows and fur, and Expand builds the full room. Manuel's trick: Kontext in Krea takes two images, so paste several references into one composite image and say what to take from each. Based on a real pet-bed brief.
how_to_use: Krea > image > Flux Kontext Pro; upload the montage; prompt with Subject + Action + Product + Setting + Vibe; use Expand for the environment.

name: AI post-production in Photoshop (layer comps, regeneration compositing, de-oversharpening)
summary: #14 'Postproduction Stravaganza' (2025-09-10; presenter Julian Garcia per the Slack recap): AI output is bitmaps, so fight for a post-production component in scoping. Save states with Photoshop layer comps for QC and before/after; use an LLM (Gemini outperforming ChatGPT) to turn a rough composite into a photoreal integration; inspect generations like newborns (eyes, hands, feet, teeth) and composite the best parts of several generations; use Nano Banana (free in Gemini, start fresh chats) to move camera or pose; remove AI oversharpening with High Pass 1-1.2 px, invert, Overlay, then mask detail back on the face. Photoshop beta Harmonize recommended.
how_to_use: Oversharpening fix: duplicate layer > Filter > Other > High Pass 1-1.2 px > Invert (Ctrl/Cmd+I) > blend mode Overlay > mask.

name: Spooky customer requests: medical before/after assets (Kiyomi Skin)
summary: Emmanuel Cantón (#21, 2025-10-29): Kiyomi Skin needed 23 medically accurate visuals plus resizes (50 assets): enhancing customers' real before/after photos (an enhancer vs Krea tests), wrinkle-reduction before/after, and a natural-elements product environment. All assets were approved and the client asked for more resizes. Team: Alex Faber (lead creative), Mina Vigliotti and Julieta Novarini (CPMs), Adelle Adrian.

name: When AI says 'Nope' (illustration)
summary: Juan Esteban Charry (#23, 2025-11-19): an illustration session on what to do when the model refuses or you can't iterate freely, worked through one task across Display, Mobile, Social and DOOH formats. AI news: EA x Stability AI, licensed McConaughey/Caine voices in ElevenLabs, Freepik Spaces, WPP Open Pro. The deck is mostly visual, so detail is limited.

name: 8-bit pixel sprite animation with Nano Banana (Salesloft Times Square ad)
summary: #26 'From Prompt to Pixel Sprite Animation' (2025-12-10): an 8-bit pixel animated ad for Salesloft on Times Square on a very tight timeline. Nano Banana generated a sprite sheet (spaceship, heart, trophy, projectiles, blocks, explosion); Nano Banana (Pro) Edit generated animation frames from a reference; frames were assembled as a GIF/image sequence in Photoshop (0.07-0.1 s per frame) and combined with traditional motion. Team: Jorge Martinez (Motion CL), Caroline Peixoto (ACD), Julian Garcia (AI ACD), Fernando Thomé, Andreina Rangel (CPM), Bianca Takahashi, David Grevler (sound).
how_to_use: Prompt: 'Create a sprite sheet of 8-bit pixel art style of the following assets...'; then Edit: 'Create frames for a sprite pixel animation of...'; select frames and set 0.07-0.1 s intervals in Photoshop.

name: Hybrid 2D AI character animation (AI motion + vectors + AE camera)
summary: Gian Orsi (#34, 2026-03-04): separate creative intent from labour, as cel animation did. Prepare Illustrator assets for AI motion, generate animated characters with AI, remove chroma with Santiago Rodriguez's chroma-remover preset (keeps detailed edges), composite with vector elements and backgrounds under an After Effects 3D camera (controlled, unlike full-AI backgrounds that hallucinate), and retime with motion curves. Saved 80-100 hours of rigging and animation; a 2D niche Superside can lead.
how_to_use: Chroma-remover preset link is in the #34 deck.

name: Figma Console MCP (Southleft)
summary: Open-source (MIT) MCP by Southleft that, unlike the official Figma MCP, gives the agent access to the whole Figma file (variables, components, styles) and can write back to it. Miguel Leça used it at #42 (2026-05-06) to assemble emails from a screenshot using design-system components.
how_to_use: Install the Figma Console MCP in your agent (Claude Code/Cursor), point it at the file, then ask it to analyse the reference, map structure and build with existing components.

name: stragentlove-starter repo template + /skillify skill
summary: Manuel Berbin's take-home kit from #65 'Dr. Stragentlove' (2026-10-15): a starter repo for agent-driven creative work (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, learnings/ layered global > client > format > project, a solved example project, a carousel-to-motion skill) plus /skillify, a skill that turns a solved problem into a shareable skill with a preflight check of required tools/MCPs.
how_to_use: Download the starter from Drive, open the folder in Claude Code, read CLAUDE.md; run /skillify after solving a problem to package it.

name: Event badge maker (vibe-coded) + Flora mockup workflow
summary: From Vitória Borba's bootcamp project (#57, 2026-08-19) for a fictional Dropbox AI conference: a vibe-coded badge maker for an event check-in totem, and a Flora mockup workflow with a brand style/vibe box, a screen/glass realism box (prompt tip: 'there is a glass over the UI, so it should behave like glass'), a mockup description and the design image.
